SK1091 The private auto-property is a field

A private auto-property generates a backing field, a getter and a setter to do what a field does directly.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

A private auto-property has no external contract to preserve: nothing outside the type can bind to it, so the property exists only to wrap a field the compiler generated anyway. What the wrapper costs is not the two accessor calls the JIT inlines away — it is that the field is invisible. readonly cannot be applied to it, ref cannot be taken of it, an Interlocked update cannot be written against it, and every one of those is a tool the author gave up without being asked. ⚠ This is `SK1003` from the other side and the two cannot both fire on one declaration. SK1003 starts from a private field with a hand-written property over it and folds the field into the field keyword; this starts from a private auto-property with no field at all and turns it into one. SK1003 requires two bodied accessors and a separate field declaration, neither of which an auto-property has.

Example

Instead of:

sealed class Cache {
    private Dictionary<string, int> Entries { get; set; } = new();
}

Write:

sealed class Cache {
    private Dictionary<string, int> Entries = new();
}

When it does not fire

⚠ The fix keeps the name. Renaming Entries to entries would be a naming decision this rule does not own and would spread the edit across every use site; leaving the identifier alone makes the rewrite entirely local, which is what fixIsSafe: true is claiming. ⚠ The `private` modifier must be written, which is also how an explicit interface implementation is excluded — those carry no accessibility modifier and cannot be private. An init accessor is declined outright, because a field cannot be set by an object initializer the way an init property can, and required with it. ⚠ The property must be both read and written somewhere in the type. A field that is never assigned is CS0649 and one that is assigned and never read is CS0414, so a fix that did not check would turn a silent property into a warning on a TreatWarningsAsErrors build — the exact failure fixIsSafe: true promises will not happen. ⚠ A get-only auto-property becomes a `readonly` field, which preserves the constructor-assignment-only contract the accessor list was expressing. ⚠ Records are excluded: with sets members positionally and by name, and the synthesized equality members are written against the fields. A type carrying [Serializable] or [StructLayout], a property carrying any attribute, and a type declared across more than one file are all declined — the first two because they mark the declarations most likely to be bound reflectively by name, and the third because the read-and-write census cannot see the other file. ⚠ Nothing upstream implements this, so there is no reference behaviour to inherit and no false-positive experience to borrow; every restriction above was derived here.
